aiOverview.content: Measles is a highly contagious, serious viral infection causing high fever, cough, red/watery eyes, and a characteristic rash. Spread through airborne droplets, it can cause severe complications like pneumonia and encephalitis, especially in children under 5. Vaccination (MMR) is the best protection, with no specific antiviral treatment available. Symptoms Initial: High fever, cough, runny nose, and red, watery eyes (conjunctivitis). Early Signs: Small white spots (Koplik spots) may appear inside the cheeks. Rash: A red, blotchy rash appears 3-5 days after initial symptoms, starting on the face and spreading downward, lasting 5-6 days. Duration: Symptoms typically appear 7–14 days after exposure. Causes and Spread Cause: The measles virus. Transmission: Highly contagious, spreading through coughing, sneezing, or close contact. The virus can live in the air or on surfaces for up to 2 hours. Contagious Period: Infected people can spread the virus 4 days before to 4 days after the rash appears. Complications Common: Ear infections and severe diarrhea. Severe: Pneumonia (common cause of death), encephalitis (brain swelling), and death. High-risk groups: Children under 5, adults over 20, pregnant individuals, and those with weakened immune systems. Treatment and Prevention Vaccination: The Measles-Mumps-Rubella (MMR) vaccine is 97% effective. Treatment: There is no specific antiviral treatment; care focuses on symptom relief, hydration, and treating complications. Prevention: Vaccination is the only effective preventative measure. Note: As of March 2026, over 1,400 cases have been reported in the US this year.
